app.description: Ledger on one Platform: createLedger hands auth-toolkit's createApp the Ledger API, the device Backend and the Session, and opens this device's Settings

app-session.description: What one signed-in user gets: a collection for each kind of their money and the Backend's commands, on the signed rpc client and the Std Sync createApp hands it

app-device.description: The device Backend: the Backend on the device's own table and the Name Token resolver, loaded as a chunk of its own on the web and bundled on a phone

app-cache.description: What only this device has, belonging to no user: its Settings and their table

app-places.description: The Place order both apps follow, every Place with its address and Go Command, the stops a Thumb Lock picks, and what each Place shows, worked out once over the open session's money

app-commands.description: The vocabulary: every Command with its keys, the gesture that gives it on a touch screen, the guide to every gesture, and the sound and Key Bar of each as it is given

backend.description: The Backend, wherever it runs: the Ledger API's handlers on the services they need, each service with a cloud and a device version, imported from its own module

backend-handlers.description: Your logic: what each Ledger API call does, for the user who signed it, on the ledger table

backend-services.description: What the handlers stand on, one folder per service: its definition, and a cloud and a device version, each imported from its own file so a Worker loads only the cloud one and the app only the device one

services.description: Each version stands on its service's definition

api.description: The Ledger API both sides speak

model.description: The words of money, Accounts, Categories, Entries and the currency, with the sums over them

ledger-core.description: Read top-down: the app on each user's Session, the device Backend, and the cache; the Backend answers the API in the words of the model. Commands stand alone; the Place order names them.
